note: Transcribed from the scan (Machen 1923 plates, January 1924 printing, p. 22): groups of verb forms of the present active indicative. Answers written for this course (every Greek form checked by build/greek_corpus.py). Machen's thou/ye are given as you (sg.)/you (pl.); the book's wording is in data.book_prompt.

items.answer: You (sg.) see, you (sg.) know, you (sg.) take.

accept: Thou seest, thou knowest, thou takest.

items.answer: He writes, he has, he says.

accept: She writes, she has, she says.

items.answer: He looses, he teaches, he sees.

accept: She looses, she teaches, she sees.

items.answer: We take, we have, we know.
You (pl.) see, you (pl.) say, you (pl.) write.

accept: Ye see, ye say, ye write.

items.answer: They teach, they take, they loose.
You (pl.) know, you (sg.) know, we know.

accept: Ye know, thou knowest, we know.

items.answer: We see, they teach, he says.
You (sg.) have, they see, we take.

accept: Thou hast, they see, we take.
